title: Evaluation of a forensic marking intervention for domestic abuse
description: The forensic marking intervention for domestic abuse aims to prevent unwanted contact and support the detection of crimes. Victims receive a forensic marking kit which when deployed, can provide evidence that a perpetrator has been in close proximity to the victim. The perpetrator is warned about the intervention with the aim of deterring them from further offending.
evaluation_methods: Quasi-experimental method; Matching; Case studies Individual interviews Surveys and polling
major_project: This intervention is not a major project

title: Evaluation of video first response (VFR) to non-emergency domestic abuse calls for service
description: Video first response (VFR) is the use of video conferencing to provide the initial police response to eligible non-emergency domestic abuse calls for service. During the video calls, the VFR officer can collect evidence, create safeguarding referrals, conduct risk assessments and may take MG11 and victim personal statements.
evaluation_methods: Quasi-experimental method Randomised control trial (RCT); Individual level RCT; Matching; Individual interviews Qualitative observational studies
major_project: This intervention is not a major project

title: Police officers in the classroom supporting the PSHE curriculum
description: This trial aims to understand whether police officers teaching PSHE lessons on sexual consent and the law improves young people's trust and confidence in the police, knowledge of consent and the law and confidence in making informed choices and reporting instances where consent is breached. The research compares police officers with teachers delivering the same intervention.
